commitResults.messageTitle: Create Task class to manage task statuses
Add Deadline task, Event task and Todo task
Add ability to save the list
Switch date and time representation from String to LocalDateTime
refactor: extract user interaction into Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
Move Kotha's welcome, command input, task-list display, task-count, goodbye, and error-output responsibilities into a dedicated Ui class. Keep command dispatch and task mutation in Kotha so this remains a small, behavior-preserving refactoring step.

Also normalize the source package declarations to kotha so the classes share one package and can be imported as kotha.Kotha.
Store the backing path per Storage instance and configure Kotha with data/kotha.txt. Handle storage files without a parent directory so the class remains reusable for tests and alternate locations.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: extract command classification into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Move command-word recognition out of Kotha into Parser.CommandType while retaining argument validation and command execution in Kotha. Preserve existing command behavior and unknown-command handling.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: extract task collection into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList to own task storage and basic collection operations. Update Kotha to load, display, mutate, and persist tasks through TaskList while preserving existing command behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: extract task mutations into TaskOperations
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a task-operation class for adding, removing, marking, and unmarking tasks. Keep command validation and coordination in Kotha while delegating state mutations to the new class.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: move task commands into TaskOperations
commitResults.messageBody: Move todo, deadline, event, delete, mark, and unmark command operations out of Kotha. TaskOperations now validates command arguments, creates and mutates tasks, reports task changes, and persists the updated list.

Replace the TaskOperations-specific exception with a package-level KothaException that can be used by Kotha and all other classes in the kotha package. Preserve the existing user-facing error messages and checked-exception flow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Change error messages to better fit Kotha's personality
Edit JavaDoc comments in Parser.java and Ui.java
refactor: move task behavior into domain classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Apply SE-EDU Java coding conventions across the task classes, correct TaskList.remove to return the removed task, and use PECS for task collection inputs and consumers.

Remove TaskOperations. Task now creates validated ToDo, Deadline, and Event instances and owns completion-state behavior, while TaskList owns collection mutations. Kotha remains responsible for command coordination, UI interaction, and persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Group task related classes in kotha.tasks package
Setup Gradle checkstyle and shadowJar plugin
Align test code with SE-EDU standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Test sources use inconsistent import ordering and formatting, which makes the project's Java style inconsistent and triggers Checkstyle.

Reorder imports, remove an unused import, use package-private test classes, fix spacing, and add the missing final newline so test code follows the project standard.

Java code needs a reusable project-level style reference so future changes follow the same conventions.

Add the Java coding skill, track project-local skill files, and require the standard from AGENTS.md.

Commit messages need a reusable project-level standard so future history stays clear and consistent.

Add the Git skill and require its conventions from AGENTS.md for all future commits.

Introduce a JavaFX chatbot-style interface for Kotha while preserving the existing command-line application. Share command processing through KothaEngine so the GUI supports task creation, listing, searching, marking, unmarking, deadlines, events, and deletion with persistent storage.

Display a bundled Kotha icon and allow users to select a profile picture for their messages. Correct the dialog layout so bot and user icons appear on their respective sides of the conversation bubbles.
Expose the profile picture chooser in the chatbot input bar so the selected user icon can be used by the conversation UI.

Use response categories to colour Kotha's message bubbles and automatically select readable text colours with a JavaFX ladder. Treat unknown commands as exceptions so their error responses use the red bubble style.
Pass the processed response category into bot dialog bubbles so each conversation message receives the appropriate colour class.

The indentation in the switch statements did not follow the Java SE-EDU
coding standard in the previous version, this has been fixed.

Furthermore there were some if statements without a {...} block which
also has been fixed

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Java Assertions to validate assumptions
refactor: separate command dispatch from processing
commitResults.messageBody: Extract command execution from KothaEngine.processCommand into executeCommand.The original method combined input parsing, response-style bookkeeping, command dispatch, task mutation, persistence, and response construction in one long method. This made the happy path harder to scan and mixed multiple abstraction levels.Keeping parsing and exception handling in processCommand while delegating the switch to a focused helper makes each method easier to understand and modify. The refactoring preserves command behavior and response text.

Reuse one private printTasks helper for the full task list and search result views.The two public methods previously duplicated the separators, task numbering loop, and output formatting, differing only in their heading. This duplication increased the chance that future display changes would be applied inconsistently.The refactoring centralizes the shared behavior while keeping the public methods expressive and preserving their existing output.

Extract task-type dispatch and field-count validation from Storage.parseTask into createTask.The original parser mixed storage-line splitting, task construction, completion-state restoration, and malformed-date handling. This made the persistence code harder to follow and increased the cost of changing one task format.The refactoring leaves parseTask responsible for orchestration and error handling while createTask owns task-shape construction. Invalid records are still ignored exactly as before.

Reuse a single addTask helper for todo, deadline, and event commands.Each branch previously duplicated insertion into the task list, persistence, and confirmation formatting. Keeping that workflow in one place reduces maintenance risk and makes the command dispatch easier to scan, while the command-specific factories and response prefixes remain explicit.No command behavior or response text has changed.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: separate application loop from dispatch
commitResults.messageBody: Extract command dispatch from Kotha.main into a processCommand helper.The main method previously combined application lifecycle control, parsing, command routing, and error handling, creating a long chain of nested branches. The refactoring leaves main responsible for reading commands and managing termination, while processCommand handles one command at a time.The helper returns an explicit exit flag so the existing bye behavior and exception handling remain unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: use enum switch for command routing
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the if-else command-routing chain in Kotha.processCommand with a switch over Parser.CommandType.Parser.CommandType is a finite enum, so switch communicates the domain model more clearly than repeated equality checks. The change makes each supported command an explicit case and leaves unknown-command handling in the default branch.Command behavior, output, and termination semantics are unchanged.

Extract mark and unmark handling from KothaEngine.executeCommand into updateTaskStatus.The dispatcher previously selected the command word, validated the task index, changed completion state, saved the list, and formatted the response in one branch. That mixed routing with operation details and used a nested conditional expression.The helper gives status updates one clear responsibility and keeps mark and unmark behavior unified without changing output or persistence semantics.

Replace persistence protocol literals with named constants in Storage.Task type codes and completion status values are part of the on-disk format, but their raw literals previously obscured their meaning and could be changed inconsistently. Naming them documents the format and gives future updates one place to modify.The serialized representation and loading behavior remain unchanged.

Replace unexplained DialogBox layout literals with named constants for label width, icon size, and content spacing.These values define visible UI dimensions, so naming them makes the layout intent clear and provides a single point of change when the design is adjusted.The numerical values and resulting interface layout remain unchanged.

Replace the repeated profile image dimension literal in MainWindow with PROFILE_IMAGE_SIZE.The value controls both image allocation and pixel initialization, so a named constant makes the intended UI dimension explicit and prevents those uses from drifting apart.The generated image size and application behavior remain unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: name task command grammar constants
commitResults.messageBody: Replace repeated task command and marker literals with named constants in Task.The command words and delimiters form the input grammar for todo, deadline, and event creation. Naming them makes substring boundaries and marker searches easier to understand, and gives future grammar changes a single source of truth.Parsing behavior and accepted command syntax remain unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: remove repeated date parsing logic
commitResults.messageBody: Extract the repeated try-catch parsing attempt from Task.parseDate into tryParseDate.The original method duplicated the same exception handling for each supported date format, making the parsing sequence noisier and easier to edit inconsistently. The refactoring makes the format fallback order explicit while retaining the final exception for invalid input.Accepted date formats and error behavior remain unchanged.

Replace raw command-word literals in Parser with named constants.The parser defines the command vocabulary used throughout routing, but the literals previously obscured that role and could be changed inconsistently. Named constants make the grammar easier to scan and maintain without changing command matching behavior.

Change Storage.loadTasks to return List<Task> instead of the concrete ArrayList type.Callers consume the result through the List abstraction, so exposing ArrayList unnecessarily couples the API to its current implementation. The method continues to build and return an ArrayList internally, preserving behavior while allowing the implementation to change independently.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: use stream for task serialization
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the manual loop in Storage.saveTasks with a stream that maps each task through formatTask.This is a direct collection transformation with no ordering or side-effect complexity, so the stream expresses the intent concisely while preserving task order and serialized output. File-system handling remains unchanged.
